abstract.text: A component that defines an entity’s behavior in physics body simulations.
Apply an impulse at a point. This immediately modifies the velocity.
It also modifies the angular velocity if the point of application is not at the center of mass. This wakes up the body.
Clear all forces. This will zero out the forces and torques.
Custom debug color.
The physics body’s material properties, like friction.
Validates atomically. Retains body identity and authored mass while updating native locks/sleep policy.
Changing initiallyAwake here does not override an existing body’s observed awake state.
Apply a torque. This affects the angular velocity without affecting the linear velocity of the center of mass. This wakes up the body.
Accumulates native force for the next step. Call once per desired step, not once per render frame.
Returns whether eligible dynamic geometry was submitted; sleeping bodies can ignore it when wake is false.
Sensors are excluded by default, and native unsupported line shapes receive no aerodynamic force.
The physics body’s mass properties, like inertia and center of mass.
Apply a force at a world point. If the force is not applied at the center of mass, it will generate a torque and affect the angular velocity. This wakes up the body.
Get the world velocity of a local point.
The physics body’s mode, indicating how or if it moves.
Apply a force to the center of mass. This wakes up the body.
Linear velocity of the center of mass.
Before simulation starts, reads and writes the initial velocity used when the body is created.
Get the world linear velocity of a world point attached to this body.
Applies an impulse at an exact global point without narrowing its world coordinates.
Explicit command; sleeping a native body can sleep its whole touching island.
Before creation, sets the authored initial state. Native sleep transitions are otherwise left alone.
A component that defines an entity’s behavior in physics body simulations.
A component whose runtime constructor metadata was generated by
. A fieldwise constructor needs an alias-specific default
factory; an
constructor can be registered directly.
Get the world position of the center of mass.
The base component in ECS paradigm.
Component contains data described some entity characteristic in the game world, like:
color, transformation and etc.
Is this body a sensor?
Validates atomically, updates an existing native body without recreation and wakes it.
Before creation, stores the settings used by the first physics sync. Invalid settings leave it unchanged.
A protocol that allows to use components and entities as query targets.
The physics body’s filter.
Set the angular velocity of a body in radians per second
Applies force at an exact global point; torque uses a precise nearby lever arm.
Set the position of the body’s origin and rotation. Manipulating a body’s transform may cause non-physical behavior.
Should this body be prevented from rotating? Useful for characters.
Teleports an existing body using exact global coordinates. Returns false for invalid input or no body.
An ECS-owned precise position should also be updated when authoritative component sync is active.
Exact global position while the native body exists. Nil before creation or after removal.
A component that exposes generated, runtime-agnostic field metadata.
